correctness.rationale: Direct inversion gives Q_r(u)=log[-log(1-u^(1/r))]. With a=-log(u), w=1-exp(-a/r), g(t)=(-log(1-t))/t strictly increasing via its positive integral derivative, Q_r'(u)=g(w)/[a*u*g(1-w)]. Increasing r strictly decreases w, hence the ratio and Q'(u); integration on every compact [u,v] subset (0,1) gives strict contraction. For D=Q_s-Q_r, D is strictly decreasing; its centered version has zero integral and positive every proper initial integral, giving strict centered convex order by the equal-mean integrated-quantile theorem, including strictly convex losses. Exponential left and double-exponential right tails guarantee all finite moments. Independent stable analytic-versus-finite-difference and grid checks passed 1,936 assertions (8 shapes, 11 quantiles), supplementary only; the universal assertion is proved analytically.
